cohort: The study retrospectively examined 252 extremely low birth weight (ELBW) infants, weighing less than 1000 g, delivered at a single hospital from April 2015 to December 2023.
finding: Successful en caul cesarean section (ECCS) for extremely low birth weight infants significantly reduced the risk of neonatal intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) grade >= 3 and did not contribute to infant anemia or hypoxia at delivery.
mod_finding: The incidence of IVH grade >= 3 was significantly lower in the group of successful ECCS compared with other delivery modes (unsuccessful ECCS, non-trial ECCS, and vaginal delivery).
